newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Assembly panel rejects 10 pct tax cut.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Assembly panel rejects 10 pct tax cut.

text.p: California Assembly members on Friday rejected Republican Gov. Pete Wilson's 10 percent business tax cut proposal, lawmakers said.

The Democrat-controlled Assembly Appropriations Committee rejected the tax cut bill on a party-line vote of 13-to-8. The committee vote blocks the governor's proposal from advancing to the Assembly floor.

The bill, introduced by Assembly Republican Leader Curt Pringle, would have reduced the state's bank and corporation tax rate by 10 percent over the next two years. The tax cut was part of Wilson's fiscal 1997-1998 budget plan.
Pringle hopes to revive the tax cut plan during the ongoing budget negotiations, spokesman John Nelson said.
Wilson's tax cut proposal had come under fire from Democrats, who warned the cuts would be a drain on the state budget. Some Democrats are seeking more targeted tax relief.
